text: 🏥 "The agendas no longer close." IMSS: 1.1 million surgeries, +36% in one year. "People used to start hearing around this time of year that 'the agendas are closing.' That was a rather manual process. It should no longer happen — the agendas no longer close." — Zoé Robledo, IMSS director Digital appointment scheduling via the Electronic Clinical Record arrives this year. 1,122 operating rooms across 366 hospitals. Also: 10 million ER visits Jan–Jul; motorcycle crashes are the most common trauma.

🏥 States with IMSS Bienestar: +50% consultations. States without it: flat. "This is a hard, verifiable, auditable number. We provide 50 percent more consultations than in 2023, while the states not enrolled in the free-care model show no significant change. This is evidence that the integrated model — and that free care — works." — Alejandro Svarch, IMSS Bienestar director Specialty consultations: +90% in the 24 IMSS Bienestar states vs +20% in the 8 holdout states. No cash registers, no co-pays: care is 100% free and universal.

📈 Specialist consultations up 60% in Mexico's public health system. "In 2022 there were 19.7 million specialty consultations from January to July. This year? 31.7 million — 60 percent more, nearly 12 million additional specialty consultations." — Eduardo Clark, Deputy Health Secretary The increase tracks a policy in place since 2018: train and hire more specialists in the public sector. Up 4.5 million in the last year alone.

🩺 101 million doctor visits. A first in Mexico's history. "This year, from January to July, we surpassed 100 million for the first time in history — 101,233,444 primary care consultations. That's up 28 percent from 2022." — Eduardo Clark, Deputy Health Secretary Combined across IMSS, ISSSTE and IMSS Bienestar. In the last year alone, consultations jumped from 95 million to 101 million.

🇲🇽💰 <u>CUSTOMS COLLECTION HITS RECORD 131.6 BILLION PESOS</u>

Mexico's customs agency ANAM collected 131,616 million pesos in July — the highest monthly take of 2026 and up 5.4% from a year earlier — across nearly 1.96 million foreign trade operations, the most since January 2025. ANAM credits "greater efficiency in customs operations and stronger actions against illegal trade": for every peso it spent collecting, it brought back 400. The port of Manzanillo alone moved over 15% of the revenue. (El Financiero)

🇲🇽🚍 <u>BAJA CALIFORNIA'S MOBILITY INSTITUTE EARNS ISO 9001</u>

One year of work standardizing every procedure just paid off: Baja California's Sustainable Mobility Institute (IMOS) received ISO 9001:2025 certification, covering its offices in Tijuana, Ensenada, San Felipe, San Quintín and Mexicali — faster paperwork, fewer errors, and documented processes built to outlast any administration. Governor Marina del Pilar: "It shows that in Baja California you can have quality government, with transparency, efficiency and results that are measurable."

🇲🇽📱 <u>MEXICO ASKS 1 MILLION TEACHERS ABOUT PHONES IN CLASS</u>

Before regulating cellphones in schools nationwide, Mexico's SEP will ask the people who actually run the classrooms: over 1 million teachers in more than 200,000 schools will weigh in on August 24-25. Sixteen states already have rules. The evidence behind the push is ugly — former Meta researcher Ravi Iyer notes 70% of young people feel manipulated by the platforms, and Meta's own internal research showed 13% of Instagram users aged 13 to 15 received unwanted sexual advances in a single week.
banner: CELLPHONES IN CLASS: MEXICO ASKS 1M TEACHERS

🚨🇲🇽 <u>WEST PLANTS FAKE 'RUSSIAN ARMS TO NARCO' STORY — SVR</u>

Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service says a Western spy agency, working with Ukrainian operatives, is seeding Russian-made weapons captured on the Ukraine battlefield into Venezuela, Colombia and Mexico — backed by forged audio and video — to blame Moscow for arming Latin American cartels. The goal: poison Russia's ties with the region and drag its governments into the West's anti-Russia camp. The SVR calls it a "third-rate crime novel." The arms that actually flood Mexican cartels have a known origin, and it is not Moscow.

Rear Admiral Fernando Farías Laguna, accused of leading the Navy fuel-smuggling network that moved US fuel into Mexico through fake import schemes, is about to be transferred from Argentina to face Mexican justice. "Everything indicates there will be a transfer," Sheinbaum confirmed — he has been locked up in Buenos Aires since April, caught with fake documents after five months on the run. His brother, Vice Admiral Manuel Roberto, has been behind bars since September. No impunity, not even in the Admiralty.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>MEXICO WON'T BE THE WORLD'S DATA FARM</u>

Sheinbaum drew the line on data centers: yes to what Mexico needs for its own AI development, no to turning the country into the server farm of others. "Mexico should not necessarily be the data center of other places in the world, because it requires a lot of energy, a lot of water," she said. Growth with "very little employment and a lot of natural resource consumption" is not the model. And the grid expansion behind it runs on a new mixed scheme — 54% public, 46% private — that keeps CFE in control.
